WHY DID SILVER47 SIGN BEFORE ITS OWN CATALYSTS? (2026-08-24, operator hypothesis: lock in the deal, raise terms later if assays hit). DISTRESS EXPLANATION IS DEAD — the deck shows Silver47 with US$33M cash and a fully-funded program; the board CHOSE this timing, so intent is a real question. STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE THEY PRESERVED OPTIONALITY: (1) 6.3% lockup vs the typical 20-30% — and the deck pie shows D&O at ~3%, so the lockup is essentially JUST INSIDERS OWN SHARES; they locked themselves and hunted no institutional lockups, which functionally hands the decision to the float; (2) small break fee US$5.7M ~3.5% = cheap to top, deal-certainty boards negotiate bigger; (3) the vote calendar (no later than Nov-15) sits AFTER the Sept-Oct assays — that calendar was chosen. MECHANISM CORRECTION (important): the BOARD CANNOT REPRICE — by signing it bound ITSELF to recommend and support. It did NOT bind shareholders. So lock-in-then-raise is not a board play; it is executed by the REGISTER declining to deliver 66.67% at a ratio assays have made stale. Board gets certainty + partner; holders keep the option. HONEST INVERSE (fits the same facts): management may have seen early core, concluded the program will not re-rate the stock, and sold the story at a 38% premium before that becomes public — insider information asymmetry runs their way and nothing known rules this out. STRONGEST SYNTHESIS: the board learned in 2026 that THE MARKET WOULD NOT PAY THEM FOR GOOD NEWS — raised at C$1.05 in Jan, drilled all summer while silver ran to $64, stock printed C$0.49. So the deal is not sell-before-assays but GET INTO A CONTAINER WHERE ASSAYS ARE VALUED (producing, TSX, 4-analyst-covered platform where an ounce fetches $2-3 vs $1); 43% of properly-priced assets beats 100% of chronically-discounted ones — and it leaves the bump option intact as a side effect. PROXY HUNT ADDITION (alongside the share-price-condition question): the BACKGROUND TO THE ARRANGEMENT section — who approached whom, timeline, whether a market check/go-shop was run — and specifically the FIDUCIARY OUT language: is there an INTERVENING EVENT clause letting the board change its recommendation for a material non-bid development? That clause is the difference between shareholders forcing a bump by threatening the vote and the board being able to actively pursue one.

DOCTRINE — IN A FIXED-RATIO ALL-SHARE DEAL, THE PREMIUM IS AN OWNERSHIP PERCENTAGE, NOT A PRICE (2026-08-24, operator asked whether the 38% is marketing fluff). FLUFF AS A PRICE: computed at one instant against an acquirer price containing ZERO deal anticipation; the announcement itself repriced BNKR ~-10%, so the C$5.38 numerator was destroyed by the release that quoted it (circular), and nobody re-issues premium now 24.8%. DURABLE VERSION — the arithmetic that does NOT decay: Silver47 UNDISTURBED US$102M vs BH US$184M = ~35.7% of combined; AT THE OFFER US$141M vs US$184M = 43.3%. The negotiation bought roughly +7.5 PERCENTAGE POINTS OF PERMANENT OWNERSHIP. That does not care where BNKR trades tomorrow, in November, or after the ramp — whatever Bunker Hill Silver is worth in 2028, AGA holders own 43% instead of ~36%. THE DOLLAR PREMIUM EVAPORATES; THE OWNERSHIP PREMIUM IS LOCKED. What was surrendered in exchange: the price certainty a cash deal or collar would have given. THE REAL QUESTION (premium is a distraction from it): 43% of WHAT — in an all-share deal you are not paid a premium, you SWAP RISKS; the correct test is do I want 43% of the combined thing more than 100% of my thing, which is what all the balance-sheet/ramp/assay work is actually answering. ADDITIONAL CRITIQUE FOR THE VOTE: the 38% was measured off C$0.674 near AGA 52-WEEK LOW — the same ratio against a C$0.90 stock prints as a 3% premium, so the headline partly measures HOW BEATEN DOWN THE TARGET WAS, not buyer generosity; note also they led with 38% spot and put the 30% 20-day VWAP second, and VWAP is the more honest figure because it smooths a single depressed close.

NO-VOTE INDIFFERENCE THRESHOLD - DERIVED (2026-08-29): NAIVE RULE (vote no if standalone > 0.1724 x BNKR) is useless because THE BAR MOVES WITH THE NEWS - a great assay lifts BNKR (its legacy holders capture 56.7pct of the discovery), inflating the very consideration you would reject. DERIVATION: A = AGA undisturbed standalone value, B = BNKR standalone, D = discovery value added; AGA holders own 43.3pct. Reject when A + D > 0.433(A+B+D) -> A + D > 0.764B. But pre-close B already embeds BNKR legacy's 56.7pct claim on D, so B -> B + 0.567D: A + D > 0.764(B + 0.567D) -> A + 0.567D > 0.764B -> D > (0.764B - A)/0.567. At the ~38pct announcement premium, 0.764B = 1.38A, giving D > 0.38A/0.567 = ~0.67A. RESULT: A NO VOTE ONLY BECOMES RATIONAL IF THE DRILLING ADDS VALUE WORTH ~2/3 OF AGA'S ENTIRE PRE-DEAL MARKET CAP - not 2/3 of the premium, 2/3 of the company; the true hurdle is ~1.8x the headline premium because each dollar of discovery nets AGA holders only ~56.7 cents of relative advantage. IMPLICATION: this is a DISCOVERY-EVENT threshold (a hole that roughly doubles a junior), NOT a good-result threshold - confirmation drilling, however pleasing, mathematically argues for TAKING the deal. Threshold shifters to price at the vote: (a) standalone FINANCING RISK raises the bar (burn ~C$2.75M/mo vs ~C$48M working capital = ~17mo runway; rejection means funding the next program alone, likely dilutive); (b) forfeited BNKR RAMP EXPOSURE (first concentrate Jun-29, zinc revenue) is real value received; (c) an INTERLOPER collapses the calculation entirely - then the standalone argument need not be won, only the asset made visible. CLOCK (config-confirmed): vote ~Nov-15-2026, assays expected September = ~8 week decision window, with leverage decaying as arbs replace natural holders with mechanical yes-votes. THE THRESHOLD IS A NUMBER; THE LEVERAGE TO ACT ON IT IS A WASTING ASSET.
